newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LEEDS TO FINE YEBOAH TWO WEEKS' WAGES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEEDS TO FINE YEBOAH TWO WEEKS' WAGES.

text.p: Ghanaian striker Tony Yeboah will be fined a fortnight's pay for ripping off his Leeds United shirt and throwing it at manager George Graham, the English premier club said on Tuesday.
"George will be disciplining him with a fine which is expected to be around two weeks' wages," club secretary Nigel Pleasants said. He declined to say how much Yeboah was paid.
Yeboah threw his shirt towards the manager's dug-out after being substituted when Leeds were beaten 1-0 at Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday.
He did not travel back to Leeds on the team coach although Graham later said he had known before the match that Yeboah would remain in London to visit relatives.
Yeboah has not seen eye to eye with Graham since December when he started training again after a cartilage operation which had kept him out for two months.
The Ghanaian, who joined Leeds from Germany's Eintracht Frankfurt for 3.4 million pounds ($5.4 million), argued he was fit to play again. Graham disagreed and kept him on the bench.
Yeboah finally returned to the first team earlier this year and has started their last four matches.
But he has failed to score in his seven appearances this season and, following Saturday's incident, it seems likely he will leave the Yorkshire club soon.
He has been linked to clubs in Germany -- including his former club Frankfurt -- and elsewhere in Europe.
